about.headline: A systems-minded mechatronics engineer.
about.copy:
Focused on developing engineering solutions that combine functionality, manufacturability and performance. Experience includes mechanical design, finite element analysis, product development and vehicle engineering through hands-on industrial projects and national-level competitions.

A strong foundation in CAD and engineering analysis is complemented by growing expertise in robotics, embedded systems and autonomous technologies. Every project is approached with an emphasis on technical accuracy, structured problem solving and continuous improvement, ensuring solutions are both innovative and practical.

With experience across design engineering, research and manufacturing environments, the objective remains consistent: to deliver reliable engineering solutions while continuously learning, adapting and contributing to multidisciplinary product development.

racing.name: E ZEALL Racing
racing.summary: Led the chassis design team for an electric go-kart, handling CAD design, structural validation, manufacturing documentation and vehicle integration for national-level competitions..
responsibilities: Designed chassis and structural components using SolidWorks
Prepared manufacturing drawings and coordinated fabrication
racing.challenge: Designing a lightweight yet strong chassis capable of withstanding front, side and rear impact loads while complying with competition regulations
racing.decision: Selected AISI 4130 Chromoly tubing and optimized the chassis geometry using finite element analysis to improve stiffness while minimizing weight.
racing.result: Successfully manufactured and validated the chassis for competition, contributing to reliable vehicle performance during national electric kart events.
racing.lesson: Learned that successful vehicle design requires balancing structural performance, manufacturability and competition constraints rather than focusing only on analysis results.

protosem.objectives: Understand the Protosem programme, learn about the team, and begin self-reflection through personality and motivation activities.
protosem.work: Participated in the kickoff session, completed the 16Personalities test, explored a relevant comic from Zen Pencils, and discussed the upcoming 20-week journey.
protosem.challenge: Getting familiar with the programme structure and understanding how to connect personal strengths with team goals.
protosem.solution: Used the personality test and comic reflection to better understand my behavior, motivations, and growth areas, while staying excited about the upcoming work.
protosem.reflection: I discovered that I am an protagonist and that my strengths include leadership, reflection, and a desire to help others. This helped me understand my personality better and how I may contribute to the team.
protosem.next: Prepare to engage actively in the coming weeks and build consistency in my learning and teamwork.

protosem.objectives: Learn workplace ethics and apply 5S principles in a practical lab environment.
protosem.work: Attended an orientation on workplace management and ethics, learned the 5S concepts of Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, and Sustain, and worked with the Electronics team to organize tools and equipment over three days.
protosem.challenge: Organizing a shared workspace efficiently while maintaining discipline, teamwork, and professionalism.
protosem.solution: Applied the 5S principles to classify, remove unnecessary items, and create a structured system for storing tools so they were easier to find and use.
protosem.mentor: Lab team mentor and workplace orientation
protosem.reflection: The 5S activity was a valuable lesson in discipline and teamwork. It taught me how small organized habits can improve efficiency and create a better working environment.
protosem.next: Continue building strong professional habits and apply structured thinking to upcoming projects and portfolio work.

protosem.objectives: Learn the basics of electronics, sensors, microcontrollers and safe prototyping.
protosem.work: Reviewed voltage, current, GPIO and breadboard wiring, then identified the components needed for an ESP32-based IoT prototype.
protosem.challenge: Connecting software concepts with unfamiliar electronic hardware.
protosem.solution: Started with simple LED and sensor circuits, documented each connection, and tested one component at a time.
protosem.reflection: Breaking the circuit into small tests made electronics feel more approachable and reduced wiring mistakes.
protosem.next: Build a local Wi-Fi LED control prototype.

protosem.objectives: Understand HTTP request-response flow and control an ESP32 output from a browser.
protosem.work: Created a local web server with ON and OFF endpoints for the onboard LED and tested the interface across the local network.
protosem.challenge: Keeping the embedded server responsive while making the browser controls clear.
protosem.solution: Separated the GPIO handlers from the interface and added a simple status response for each command.
protosem.reflection: The first working endpoint showed how quickly a physical device can become an interactive web product.
protosem.next: Improve status feedback and document the wiring and test results.

protosem.objectives: Build a reliable local IoT control interface with clear device feedback.
protosem.work: Refined the LED web panel, tested repeated commands, and added polling so the interface reflects the device state.
protosem.challenge: Handling delayed responses and avoiding a mismatch between the UI and the physical LED.
protosem.solution: Used a dedicated status endpoint and regular state checks instead of relying only on button clicks.
protosem.reflection: A useful IoT interface must communicate the device state, not just send commands.
protosem.next: Move from local HTTP control to cloud messaging with MQTT.

protosem.objectives: Understand MQTT publish-subscribe architecture and connect an ESP32 to a cloud feed.
protosem.work: Configured an MQTT feed, published test values, and observed messages arriving at the ESP32 subscriber.
protosem.challenge: Understanding the difference between a direct HTTP request and broker-based messaging.
protosem.solution: Mapped the publisher, broker, topic and subscriber roles before implementing the relay command.
protosem.reflection: MQTT makes the system more flexible because the sender and device do not need to know each other directly.
protosem.next: Connect the MQTT message to a low-voltage relay test circuit.

protosem.objectives: Control a relay through MQTT and understand safe separation between control logic and load wiring.
protosem.work: Tested ON and OFF messages with a relay module and documented the low-voltage control side before connecting a demonstration load.
protosem.challenge: Maintaining electrical safety while validating the switching behaviour.
protosem.solution: Used a low-voltage test setup first and treated the relay as an isolated interface between ESP32 logic and the load.
protosem.reflection: Hardware demonstrations need the same discipline as software tests, especially when a load is involved.
protosem.next: Add a voice-triggered control layer.

protosem.objectives: Connect voice commands to the IoT system using webhooks and an automation service.
protosem.work: Mapped a voice phrase through an automation trigger and webhook into the cloud feed used by the ESP32.
protosem.challenge: Tracing failures across several services instead of one local program.
protosem.solution: Tested each boundary independently: voice trigger, webhook request, cloud feed, MQTT message and relay response.
protosem.reflection: A distributed system is easier to debug when every handoff has a visible test and expected result.
protosem.next: Document the complete voice-to-device architecture.

protosem.objectives: Begin a combined smart-home prototype with environmental sensing and remote control.
protosem.work: Planned the ESP32 architecture, selected temperature, humidity and light sensors, and defined the data fields for the cloud database.
protosem.challenge: Combining control, sensing and cloud data without making the first prototype too complex.
protosem.solution: Defined a small data model and separated sensor readings, appliance state and settings into clear groups.
protosem.reflection: Planning the data model early helps hardware and dashboard work evolve together.
protosem.next: Implement the sensor reading loop and cloud connection.

protosem.objectives: Read environmental sensors reliably and prepare telemetry for cloud storage.
protosem.work: Connected the DHT11 and LDR, tested repeated readings, and added basic smoothing for the analog light value.
protosem.challenge: Sensor values fluctuate and can make automation decisions unstable.
protosem.solution: Sampled the light sensor repeatedly and used an averaged value before sending telemetry.
protosem.reflection: Good automation depends on interpreting sensor data rather than reacting to every raw reading.
protosem.next: Send telemetry to Firebase and verify the stored structure.

protosem.objectives: Store sensor readings and appliance state in a real-time cloud database.
protosem.work: Configured Firebase authentication and database paths for telemetry, bulb state, operating mode and light threshold.
protosem.challenge: Keeping cloud data structured enough for both firmware and dashboard clients.
protosem.solution: Used predictable paths and tested reads and writes with small known values before connecting the full loop.
protosem.reflection: The database becomes part of the system architecture, not just a place to store data after the fact.
protosem.next: Build the first dashboard view for live telemetry.

protosem.objectives: Create a web dashboard that displays live temperature, humidity, light and relay state.
protosem.work: Designed dashboard cards and connected them to Firebase listeners for real-time updates.
protosem.challenge: Presenting changing sensor data without creating a noisy or confusing interface.
protosem.solution: Grouped related readings, used clear units, and separated current state from historical records.
protosem.reflection: The dashboard is most useful when it helps a person make a decision quickly.
protosem.next: Add manual control, automatic mode and threshold settings.

protosem.objectives: Implement manual and automatic appliance control from the dashboard.
protosem.work: Added a relay toggle, operating-mode switch and configurable light threshold connected to the shared database.
protosem.challenge: Preventing manual commands and automatic rules from fighting each other.
protosem.solution: Made the selected mode explicit and applied automatic decisions only when automatic mode is active.
protosem.reflection: Explicit system modes make behaviour easier to explain, test and trust.
protosem.next: Test edge cases and reconnect behaviour.

protosem.objectives: Test the smart-home system across sensor, cloud, dashboard and relay boundaries.
protosem.work: Ran end-to-end tests for telemetry updates, relay commands, mode changes and temporary network interruptions.
protosem.challenge: Finding whether a failure came from hardware, Wi-Fi, cloud data or the browser.
protosem.solution: Logged each stage with timestamps and tested the system layer by layer before repeating the full workflow.
protosem.reflection: System-level testing turns a collection of working parts into evidence of a working product.
protosem.next: Improve error states and add a simple data export.

protosem.objectives: Improve the dashboard experience and make sensor history useful for analysis.
protosem.work: Added clearer loading and offline states, reviewed the telemetry schema, and planned CSV export for recorded readings.
protosem.challenge: Showing useful history without overwhelming the main control view.
protosem.solution: Kept live controls prominent and moved detailed records into an exportable data view.
protosem.reflection: A polished interface communicates system limits as clearly as system capabilities.
protosem.next: Prepare a technical demonstration and portfolio documentation.

protosem.objectives: Document the IoT prototype with architecture, wiring, code and test evidence.
protosem.work: Organized the system into hardware, cloud and dashboard layers and prepared placeholders for photos, diagrams and demonstration videos.
protosem.challenge: Turning a hands-on build into a clear story that another engineer can follow.
protosem.solution: Documented the signal flow from sensor or user command to cloud state, firmware action and visible result.
protosem.reflection: Documentation exposes gaps that are easy to miss while focusing only on getting the prototype to work.
protosem.next: Capture final build evidence and review the project critically.

protosem.objectives: Evaluate reliability, safety and maintainability of the connected system.
protosem.work: Reviewed power, relay isolation, credentials, failure recovery and the clarity of the firmware and dashboard structure.
protosem.challenge: Balancing a working demonstration with responsible engineering practice.
protosem.solution: Listed risks separately from features and identified improvements needed before real-world deployment.
protosem.reflection: A prototype is valuable when it makes the next engineering decision clearer, including what should not ship yet.
protosem.next: Apply the highest-impact improvements and retest.

protosem.objectives: Refine the prototype based on testing evidence and prepare a repeatable setup.
protosem.work: Simplified setup steps, reviewed naming and configuration values, and repeated the main workflow from a clean starting point.
protosem.challenge: Avoiding undocumented steps that only work on the original development setup.
protosem.solution: Created a concise checklist for hardware, firmware, cloud configuration and dashboard launch.
protosem.reflection: Repeatability is an important bridge between a personal experiment and a shareable engineering project.
protosem.next: Create the final walkthrough and portfolio summary.

protosem.objectives: Present the IoT system clearly through a concise technical walkthrough.
protosem.work: Prepared the project narrative from local control to cloud automation and selected the most useful evidence for each stage.
protosem.challenge: Explaining technical depth without losing the main user and system story.
protosem.solution: Focused the walkthrough on problem, architecture, decision, result and next improvement.
protosem.reflection: The strongest project explanation shows both what was built and why each design choice mattered.
protosem.next: Collect feedback and identify the next version of the system.

protosem.objectives: Review feedback, consolidate learning and define practical next steps for connected systems.
protosem.work: Reviewed the build against the original objectives and recorded improvements for hardware packaging, security, scalability and user experience.
protosem.challenge: Choosing realistic improvements instead of expanding the scope without evidence.
protosem.solution: Ranked next steps by user value, technical risk and effort.
protosem.reflection: The project taught me to treat connected products as complete systems with users, data, hardware and operational constraints.
protosem.next: Publish the documentation and carry the strongest practices into future robotics work.

protosem.objectives: Close the Protosem cycle by reflecting on growth, evidence and future engineering direction.
protosem.work: Summarized the learning journey across teamwork, electronics, IoT, robotics and technical communication, then organized the final portfolio evidence.
protosem.challenge: Turning many activities into a focused account of measurable growth.
protosem.solution: Connected each milestone to a skill, a piece of evidence and one future application.
protosem.reflection: The cycle strengthened my confidence in learning unfamiliar systems through structured experiments, documentation and iteration.
protosem.next: Continue developing robotics and autonomous systems projects with stronger IoT and embedded foundations.
